"""
MPR dialogs (from the original mpr_gui.py):

* :class:`ProcessingDialog` — switch on skull strip / z-score / connected
  components and set their parameters (they always run in that order)
* :class:`AnnotationCompareDialog` — the secondary series' own annotation
  next to the primary's annotation transferred onto it, on one shared
  slice control, with the whole-volume Dice and per-slice IoU
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Optional

import numpy as np
from matplotlib.backends.backend_qt5agg import FigureCanvasQTAgg
from matplotlib.figure import Figure
from PyQt5.QtCore import Qt
from PyQt5.QtWidgets import (QCheckBox, QComboBox, QDialog, QDoubleSpinBox, QFormLayout, QGroupBox, QHBoxLayout,
                             QSlider, QSpinBox, QVBoxLayout, QWidget)

from ....core import mpr
from ....core import processing as vproc
from ...qt_utils import label, make_button


class ProcessingDialog(QDialog):
    def __init__(self, config: vproc.PipelineConfig, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.setWindowTitle("Volume Processing Pipeline")
        self.setMinimumWidth(460)
        self.result_config: Optional[vproc.PipelineConfig] = None
        layout = QVBoxLayout(self)
        layout.setContentsMargins(18, 16, 18, 14)
        layout.addWidget(label(vproc.gpu_status_text(), "Value", wrap=True))
        layout.addWidget(label("Steps always apply in this order when turned on: Skull Strip → Z-Score → "
                               "Connected Components. Turn on any subset.", "Muted", wrap=True))

        self.ss_group = QGroupBox("1. Skull Strip")
        self.ss_group.setCheckable(True)
        self.ss_group.setChecked(config.skull_strip.enabled)
        ss = QFormLayout(self.ss_group)
        self.ss_method = QComboBox()
        for method in vproc.SkullStripMethod:
            text = method.value + ("  [not installed]" if method is vproc.SkullStripMethod.HD_BET
                                   and not vproc.HAVE_HDBET else "")
            self.ss_method.addItem(text, method)
        self.ss_method.setCurrentIndex(list(vproc.SkullStripMethod).index(config.skull_strip.method))
        self.ss_peel = QDoubleSpinBox()
        self.ss_peel.setRange(0.0, 60.0)
        self.ss_peel.setValue(config.skull_strip.peel_mm)
        self.ss_peel.setSuffix(" mm")
        self.ss_peel.setToolTip("Classical method: how far inward to erode the head mask to remove "
                                "scalp / skull / CSF.")
        ss.addRow("Method", self.ss_method)
        ss.addRow("Peel depth (classical)", self.ss_peel)
        layout.addWidget(self.ss_group)

        self.z_group = QGroupBox("2. Z-Score Normalization")
        self.z_group.setCheckable(True)
        self.z_group.setChecked(config.zscore.enabled)

* Display     resampling algorithm, 3D colormap
* Processing  skull strip -> z-score -> connected components (any subset)

import re
fixes = {
 "dicomdoodle/ui/widgets/batch_panel.py": ["QLabel"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/widgets/info_panel.py": ["List"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/dialogs/label_editor.py": ["QLabel", "readable_text_color"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/dialogs/progress_dialog.py": ["Optional"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/dialogs/results_dialog.py": ["QWidget"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/dialogs/help_viewer.py": ["Optional"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/main/actions.py": ["QMenu"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/tools/viewer3d/controls.py": ["replace"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/tools/viewer3d/view.py": ["Qt"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/tools/viewer3d/window.py": ["Optional", "DicomSeries"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/tools/mpr/panels.py": ["Optional"],
 "dicomdoodle/ui/tools/mpr/window.py": ["QLabel"],
}
for path, names in fixes.items():
    src = open(path).read()
    # operate on the import block only (top of file up to first def/class)
    cut = min(i for i in (src.find("\nclass "), src.find("\ndef "), len(src)) if i >= 0)
    head, tail = src[:cut], src[cut:]
    for name in names:
        # remove ", name" or "name, " inside from-imports (multi-line aware)
        new = re.sub(rf"(import\s*\(?[^)]*?)\b{name}\b,\s*", r"\1", head, count=1)
        if new == head:
            new = re.sub(rf",\s*\b{name}\b(?=[\s,)\n])", "", head, count=1)
        assert new != head, (path, name)
        head = new
    # drop now-empty "from x import" lines like "from typing import \n"
    head = re.sub(r"^from [\w.]+ import\s*\n", "", head, flags=re.M)
    open(path, "w").write(head + tail)
# results_dialog: remove bare "import os"
p = "dicomdoodle/ui/dialogs/results_dialog.py"
s = open(p).read().replace("import os\n\n", "\n", 1); open(p, "w").write(s)
print("done")
EOF

I'll switch these to bound methods, which do auto-disconnect, so now I'm locating every affected connection.

import sys

    sig = pyqtSignal()

from PyQt5.QtCore import QObject, pyqtSignal, QEvent, QCoreApplication
from PyQt5.QtWidgets import QApplication, QWidget

class Hub(QObject):
    sig = pyqtSignal()
hub = Hub()
class W(QWidget):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        hub.sig.connect(self.on_sig)                       # bound method
        hub.sig.connect(lambda: print("lambda called; deleted =", sip.isdeleted(self)))
    def on_sig(self):
        print("bound method called")
w = W()
w.deleteLater(); QCoreApplication.sendPostedEvents(None, QEvent.DeferredDelete)
print("C++ deleted:", sip.isdeleted(w))
hub.sig.emit()
print("done")

> *Thinking:* Confirmed the fix: bound-method slots are skipped on delete, but lambda connections still fire on dead widgets. I'll convert those connections to bound methods, apply the same fix to the ontology window's background-task callbacks, and add a global exception hook so slot errors get logged instead of crashing the app.

     return gui
 
 
+def _install_exception_hook() -> None:
+    """Log and report unexpected errors instead of letting PyQt abort the app."""
+    log = logging.getLogger("dicomdoodle")
+    state = {"showing": False}
+
+    def hook(exc_type, exc, tb):
+        if issubclass(exc_type, KeyboardInterrupt):
+            sys.__excepthook__(exc_type, exc, tb)
+            return
+        details = "".join(traceback.format_exception(exc_type, exc, tb))
+        if issubclass(exc_type, RuntimeError) and "has been deleted" in str(exc):
+            log.debug("Ignored a callback into a closed window: %s", exc)
+            return
+        sys.stderr.write(details)
+        log.error("Unexpected error: %s: %s", exc_type.__name__, exc)
+        if state["showing"]:
+            return
+        state["showing"] = True
+        try:
+            from .ui.qt_utils import show_error
+            show_error(QApplication.activeWindow(), "Unexpected error",
+                       f"{exc_type.__name__}: {exc}\n\nYour work is still open; please save it.", details)
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+        finally:
+            state["showing"] = False
+
+    sys.excepthook = hook
+
+

import os, sys, glob, copy, numpy as np, pydicom
S = sys.argv[1]
files = sorted(glob.glob(S + "/sample_ax/*.dcm"))
files = [f for f in files if "_seg" not in f]
dss = sorted((pydicom.dcmread(f) for f in files), key=lambda d: int(d.InstanceNumber))
stack = np.stack([d.pixel_array[::4, ::4] for d in dss]).astype(dss[0].pixel_array.dtype)
mf = copy.deepcopy(dss[0])
mf.NumberOfFrames = len(dss); mf.Rows, mf.Columns = stack.shape[1:]
mf.PixelSpacing = [float(mf.PixelSpacing[0]) * 4, float(mf.PixelSpacing[1]) * 4]
mf.PixelData = stack.tobytes()
mf.save_as(S + "/mf/multiframe_test.dcm")
print("multi-frame:", stack.shape, pydicom.dcmread(S + "/mf/multiframe_test.dcm").pixel_array.shape)
EOF

<details>
<summary>00:24 · Write: DicomDoodle_App/README.md (115 lines)</summary>

`/data2/icmr/pushp/DicomDoodle/DicomDoodle_App/README.md`

````markdown
# DicomDoodle 2 — modular application

A redesigned DicomDoodle with a modern interface, light and dark themes,
unlimited custom labels, and a code base split into small, focused modules.
Every feature of the original tool is here, and annotation files are fully
compatible with the original: same `<slice>_seg.dcm` DICOM Segmentation
files, same segment names, same pixel content.

## Run it

```bash
cd DicomDoodle/DicomDoodle_App
pip install -r requirements.txt      # once
python main.py                       # or: python main.py "path/to/dicom folder"
```

The AI model weights (`sam2.1_l.pt`, `best_flair.pt`, `yoloe-11l-seg-pf.pt`),
the logo images and the PDF manual are found automatically in the parent
`DicomDoodle/` folder — nothing is copied. Another weights folder can be
chosen in **File ▸ Preferences ▸ AI Models**.

Preferences (theme, your labels, recent folders, window layout) are stored in
`~/.config/DicomDoodle/settings.json` (Linux), `%APPDATA%\DicomDoodle\settings.json`
(Windows) or `~/Library/Application Support/DicomDoodle/settings.json` (macOS).

## What's new for users

| Area | Original | DicomDoodle 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layout | three rows of 20 buttons | toolbar + menus, side panels for labels, display, batch ranges and series info |
| Theme | fixed light gradient | **dark and light theme** (Ctrl+T), image views always dark |
| Labels | six fixed color buttons | six built-in labels **plus your own labels in any color** (full color palette), keys 1–9, import/export |
| Responsiveness | AI ran on the GUI thread (window froze) | AI, saving and batch jobs run in the background with progress, time left and **Cancel** |
| Unsaved work | lost when changing slice | kept per slice, multi-level undo/redo, “unsaved” markers, prompt before closing |
| Overview | — | slice timeline showing saved slices, files on disk, unsaved edits and the batch ranges |
| Safety | silently overwrote earlier `_seg.dcm` | asks before replacing files from earlier sessions (can be turned off) |
| Feedback | console prints | toasts, activity log, status bar (cursor value, zoom, AI status) |
| Saved annotations | — | shown as a faint layer on each slice; all viewers zoom and pan |

Also fixed along the way: the original could crash when a source DICOM lacked
FrameOfReferenceUID or SoftwareVersions; the overlay viewer showed “Magenta”
annotations as nothing; multi-label annotation files were skipped by the
volume calculator and spread over neighbouring slices in the 3D viewer; the
app failed to start without `ontoportal_client`; “Definition and synonyms”
always showed the last search result; opening a second tool could close the first.

## Keyboard & mouse (main window)

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl+O / Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S | open folder / save slice / save all modified slices |
| Mouse wheel, ← → ↑ ↓, PgUp/PgDn, Home/End | change slice |
| Left-drag on the image | draw a SAM box (drag to move, corners to resize) |

import os
import sys
import tempfile

import numpy as np
import pydicom
from pydicom.dataset import FileDataset, FileMetaDataset
from pydicom.uid import ExplicitVRLittleEndian, MRImageStorage, generate_uid

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from dicomdoodle.core import mask_ops  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.annotation import AnnotationSession, SliceAnnotation  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.dicom_series import DicomSeries, SegFileFilter, seg_path_for  # noqa: E402

from dicomdoodle.core.seg_io import read_segmentation, write_segmentation  # noqa: E402

SIZE, SLICES = 64, 4


def make_series(folder: str) -> None:
    """Write SLICES synthetic axial MR slices (out of order on disk)."""
    study, series, frame = generate_uid(), generate_uid(), generate_uid()
    for k in reversed(range(SLICES)):
        meta = FileMetaDataset()
        meta.MediaStorageSOPClassUID = MRImageStorage
        meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID = generate_uid()
        meta.TransferSyntaxUID = ExplicitVRLittleEndian
        ds = FileDataset(None, {}, file_meta=meta, preamble=b"\0" * 128)
        ds.SOPClassUID, ds.SOPInstanceUID = MRImageStorage, meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID
        ds.StudyInstanceUID, ds.SeriesInstanceUID, ds.FrameOfReferenceUID = study, series, frame
        ds.Modality, ds.PatientName, ds.PatientID = "MR", "Test^Patient", "T1"
        ds.Manufacturer, ds.ManufacturerModelName = "Test", "Synthetic"
        ds.InstanceNumber = k + 1
        ds.ImagePositionPatient = [0.0, 0.0, float(k)]
        ds.ImageOrientationPatient = [1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]
        ds.PixelSpacing, ds.SliceThickness = [0.5, 0.5], 2.0
        ds.Rows = ds.Columns = SIZE
        ds.SamplesPerPixel, ds.PhotometricInterpretation = 1, "MONOCHROME2"
        ds.BitsAllocated, ds.BitsStored, ds.HighBit, ds.PixelRepresentation = 16, 16, 15, 0
        pixels = (np.arange(SIZE * SIZE, dtype=np.uint16).reshape(SIZE, SIZE) + k * 10)
        ds.PixelData = pixels.tobytes()
        ds.save_as(os.path.join(folder, f"slice_{k + 1}.dcm"), enforce_file_format=True)


def square_outline(shape, lo=20, hi=40):
    mask = np.zeros(shape, bool)
    mask[lo:hi, lo:hi] = True
    return mask


def test_label_rules():
    reg = LabelRegistry()
    assert [lab.value for lab in reg.labels()] == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

---
name: dicomdoodle-v2-app
description: DicomDoodle 2 modular PyQt5 rewrite in DicomDoodle/DicomDoodle_App — layout, how to test it headlessly, pitfalls found
metadata:
  type: project
---

DicomDoodle 2 (built 2026-10-27) lives in `/data2/icmr/pushp/DicomDoodle/DicomDoodle_App/` (`python main.py`, package `dicomdoodle/` with core/ workers/ ui/; README.md has the module map). The original flat scripts (DicomDoodle.py, mpr_gui.py …) are kept unchanged; the original repo already had uncommitted CRLF/import edits in DicomDoodle.py, utils.py etc. before this work — not ours, leave them.

**Why:** user asked for an advanced GUI (dark/light theme, unlimited custom labels with full color palette) split into small modules, keeping every original feature and `_seg.dcm` compatibility (writer verified byte-equivalent in pixel data + segment metadata vs original `utils.create_dicom_segmentation`).

**How to apply:**
- Test env: base anaconda `python` (3.11) has PyQt5/VTK/highdicom/ultralytics; lacks PyMuPDF and ontoportal_client (a scratch venv with `--system-site-packages` works for PyMuPDF). Its torch can't use the A40 GPUs → SAM ≈ 4 s/slice on CPU.
- GUI tests: `xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1600x1000x24"` (VTK renders via Mesa); set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` to scratch so the real settings.json isn't touched; send QTest keys to `window.windowHandle()` — QWidget key clicks bypass QShortcut.
- Pitfalls already fixed, keep the rules: connect long-lived signals (themeChanged, labelsChanged) to bound methods, never lambdas (PyQt aborts after the window is deleted); `run_task(fn, …)` passes the progress context as fn's FIRST arg; VTK `Dolly()` needs `ResetCameraClippingRange()`.
- Sample data for tests: copy slices from `T1 CONTRAST/RECON AX 3D T1 FS+C 159` to scratch; never write SEGs into the user's data folders. Related: [[avm-3d-dsa-vessel-apps]], [[jiim-sam-comparison]].

python main.py
```
It finds the model files, logo and PDF manual in the main `DicomDoodle/` folder, so nothing was copied. Your original files are untouched and nothing is committed. Git does show 9 changed files in the old folder, but they were already changed before I started (mostly line endings).

**How the code is organised**

There are 86 small files and the largest is about 660 lines. `README.md` lists every module and gives short rules for adding to the code.
- `core/`: DICOM loading, labels, saving `_seg.dcm` files, the AI models and the calculations. No GUI code, so it can be used from plain scripts.
- `workers/`: background jobs, so the window doesn't freeze while the AI or a batch runs.
- `ui/`: the theme, icons and widgets, the main window (split into window, actions, annotation, batch and tools), and one folder or file per tool window.

**What the user gets**
- **Labels:** the 6 original labels are always there and can't be changed. "Add label" opens a full colour palette, and it warns you about a duplicate name or a colour too close to an existing one. Your labels are saved between sessions, keys 1–9 select a label, and label lists can be imported and exported.
- **Dark and light themes:** switch with Ctrl+T or the toolbar. The image area stays dark in both.
- **No more freezing:** AI detection, saving and batch jobs run in the background, with progress, time left and a Cancel button.
- **Work isn't lost:** each slice keeps its own annotation when you change slice, with undo and redo. You're asked before closing with unsaved work, and before overwriting `_seg.dcm` files from earlier sessions.
- **Easier to follow:** a slice bar marks saved slices and shows the batch ranges. Ranges you set are shown on screen (the original only printed them to the console), and saved annotations appear faintly on each slice.
- **Every original tool is here:** Manual Draw, the Annotated Viewer with ontology search, the 3D viewer, the Multiplanar view, the Volume Calculator and the Multi-frame Converter.

**Compatibility:** I compared the new save code against your original `create_dicom_segmentation`. The pixel data and segment details came out identical.

**Original bugs I fixed along the way**
- The volume calculator skipped slices that have more than one label.
- In the 3D viewer, the second label of a slice appeared on the next slice.
- Magenta annotations were invisible in the Annotated Viewer.
- The app wouldn't start without the `ontoportal_client` package (it now works without it).
- Opening a second tool window could close the first.
- Saving could crash on DICOM files missing a few header fields.

The README lists the rest.

**Things that now behave differently**
- SAM now sees the clean image; the original showed it the image with earlier outlines drawn on it, so results can differ slightly.
- Batch runs ask "Replace or Skip?" when a slice already has a `_seg.dcm` from an earlier session.
- Manual Draw has both "Save" and "Save & Close".

**What I couldn't test here**
- GPU speed: the PyTorch here can't use CUDA, so SAM took about 4 seconds per slice on CPU.
- Windows-only details, such as the dark window title bar.
- The ANTsPy and HD-BET options in the Multiplanar view.

The in-app PDF manual needs `PyMuPDF`, which is in your requirements; without it the app opens the PDF in your normal viewer.

Screenshots from my test runs are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-data2-icmr-pushp/f56fc872-2e32-4328-96b4-1adda3072ea1/scratchpad/shots/` if you want to look before running it.

```python
"""
A synthetic demo series: an MRI-like head phantom with one lesion.

It lets new users practise every step of DicomDoodle without real patient
data, and it is used to make the screenshots of the User Guide. Nothing in
it comes from a real person.

    folder = ensure_demo_series(base_dir)       # writes 40 axial slices once
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import os
from typing import Tuple

import numpy as np
import pydicom
from pydicom.dataset import FileDataset, FileMetaDataset
from pydicom.uid import ExplicitVRLittleEndian, MRImageStorage, generate_uid
from scipy import ndimage

DEMO_FOLDER_NAME = "DicomDoodle demo series"
SLICES, SIZE = 40, 256
PIXEL_SPACING, SLICE_THICKNESS = 0.9375, 3.0


def phantom_volume(slices: int = SLICES, size: int = SIZE, seed: int = 7) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """(volume (z, y, x) int16, lesion mask (z, y, x) bool) of a T1-contrast-like head."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    z, y, x = np.mgrid[0:slices, 0:size, 0:size].astype(np.float32)
    zc, cy, cx = slices / 2.0, size * 0.5, size * 0.5

    head = ((x - cx) / (0.36 * size)) ** 2 + ((y - cy) / (0.44 * size)) ** 2 \
        + ((z - zc) / (0.78 * slices)) ** 2 <= 1.0
    plane = np.zeros((1, 3, 3), bool)
    plane[0] = True                                   # erode in-plane only
    inner = lambda mask, n: ndimage.binary_erosion(mask, structure=plane, iterations=n)  # noqa: E731
    skin = head & ~inner(head, 3)
    skull = inner(head, 3) & ~inner(head, 8)
    brain_outer = inner(head, 10)
    csf = inner(head, 8) & ~brain_outer

    # cortex ribbon with a wavy inner border, white matter inside
    angle = np.arctan2(y - cy, x - cx)
    depth = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(brain_outer, sampling=(10.0, 1.0, 1.0))
    ribbon = 5.0 + 2.5 * np.sin(angle * 9.0 + z * 0.4)
    gray = brain_outer & (depth <= ribbon)
    white = brain_outer & (depth > ribbon)

    vol = np.zeros((slices, size, size), np.float32)
    texture = ndimage.gaussian_filter(rng.standard_normal(vol.shape), (0.6, 2.5, 2.5)) * 160
    vol[skin] = 880
    vol[skull] = 110
    vol[csf] = 240
    vol[gray] = 610 + texture[gray] * 0.6
    vol[white] = 820 + texture[white] * 0.4

    # lateral ventricles (dark) in the middle slices
    for side in (-1, 1):
        ventricle = (((x - (cx + side * 0.055 * size)) / (0.035 * size)) ** 2
… 86 lines omitted …

import json, urllib.request, urllib.parse
def crossref(doi):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"https://api.crossref.org/works/{urllib.parse.quote(doi)}", timeout=30) as r:
        m = json.load(r)["message"]
    authors = [f"{a.get('family','')}, {''.join(p[0] + '.' for p in a.get('given','').replace('-', ' ').split())}" for a in m.get("author", [])]
    year = (m.get("published-print") or m.get("published-online") or m.get("issued"))["date-parts"][0][0]
    return dict(doi=doi, year=year, title=m["title"][0], journal=(m.get("container-title") or [""])[0],
                volume=m.get("volume"), issue=m.get("issue"), page=m.get("page"), n_auth=len(authors), first=authors[:3])
for doi in ["10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2", "10.1118/1.3611983", "10.1007/s10278-022-00683-y", "10.3389/fninf.2013.00045",

            "10.1002/hbm.24750", "10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.09.025"]:
    try:
        print(crossref(doi))
    except Exception as e:
        print(doi, "ERROR", e)
EOF

"""
The bibliography shown under Help ▸ References & Citations.

Each entry was checked against Crossref / arXiv / the project's own citation
file. ``Reference.text()`` gives an APA-style citation and ``bibtex()`` a
BibTeX entry.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Tuple

from .. import APP_NAME, APP_VERSION, AUTHOR

REPOSITORY_URL = "https://github.com/pushplochan/DicomDoodle"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reference:
    key: str                      # BibTeX key
    component: str                # what DicomDoodle uses
    role: str                     # why it matters in DicomDoodle
    authors: Tuple[str, ...]      # "Family, I. N." — already in citation order
    year: str
    title: str
    venue: str                    # journal, proceedings, publisher or "[Computer software]"
    details: str = ""             # "585(7825), 357–362"
    doi: str = ""
    url: str = ""
    kind: str = "article"         # article | inproceedings | software | book | misc
    et_al: bool = False           # author list shortened

    @property
    def link(self) -> str:
        return f"https://doi.org/{self.doi}" if self.doi else self.url

    def author_text(self) -> str:
        names = list(self.authors)
        if self.et_al:
            return ", ".join(names) + ", et al."
        if len(names) == 1:
            return names[0]
        return ", ".join(names[:-1]) + ", & " + names[-1]

    def text(self) -> str:
        """APA-style citation as plain text."""
        venue = self.venue + (f", {self.details}" if self.details else "")
        return f"{self.author_text()} ({self.year}). {self.title}. {venue}. {self.link}".replace("..", ".")

    def bibtex(self) -> str:
        authors = " and ".join(a.replace(",", ",", 1) for a in self.authors) + (" and others" if self.et_al else "")
        fields = [("author", authors), ("title", "{" + self.title + "}"), ("year", self.year)]
        if self.kind == "article":
            fields.append(("journal", self.venue))
        elif self.kind == "inproceedings":
            fields.append(("booktitle", self.venue))
        elif self.kind == "book":
            fields.append(("publisher", self.venue))
        else:
            fields.append(("howpublished", self.venue))

"""
Turns a guide chapter written in a small markup into HTML for QTextBrowser,
colored with the current theme.

Blocks (one per line):
    ## Heading   /   ### Subheading
    plain lines              paragraph (a blank line ends it)
    1. text                  numbered step
    - text                   bullet
    > TIP: text              callout box: TIP, NOTE, IMPORTANT or TRY IT
                             (following "> " lines continue the same box)
    ![Caption](shot:name)    screenshot (dicomdoodle/assets/guide/name.png)
    ![Caption](diagram:x)    diagram drawn by ui/guide/diagrams.py
    | a | b |                table row (the first row is the header)

Inline:
    **bold**  *italic*  `file name`  [[Ctrl+S]] key  {icon:save} toolbar icon
    {n:3} numbered marker (as drawn on the screenshots)
    [text](chapter:id)  [text](action:name)  [text](https://...)

Images are referenced by URL (e.g. ``shot:overview@760``); the guide window
supplies them in ``loadResource`` at exactly the requested width.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import re
from typing import Callable, List, Optional, Tuple

from ..theme import Theme, rgba

SizeOf = Callable[[str], Tuple[int, int]]          # "shot:name" -> natural (w, h)

CALLOUTS = {   # kind -> (icon, theme token)
    "TIP": ("sparkles", "accent"),
    "NOTE": ("info", "text_muted"),
    "IMPORTANT": ("alert", "warning"),
    "TRY IT": ("play", "success"),
}


def stylesheet(theme: Theme) -> str:
    return f"""
        body {{ color: {theme.text}; }}
        h1 {{ font-size: 21pt; font-weight: 700; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 2px; }}
        h2 {{ font-size: 14.5pt; font-weight: 700; margin-top: 24px; margin-bottom: 6px; }}
        h3 {{ font-size: 11.5pt; font-weight: 700; margin-top: 16px; margin-bottom: 4px; }}
        p {{ margin-top: 4px; margin-bottom: 8px; line-height: 145%; }}
        li {{ margin-bottom: 5px; line-height: 140%; }}
        a {{ color: {theme.accent}; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 600; }}
        .muted {{ color: {theme.text_muted}; }}
        .caption {{ color: {theme.text_muted}; font-size: 9pt; }}
        .eyebrow {{ color: {theme.accent}; font-size: 8.5pt; font-weight: 700; }}
    """


class Renderer:
    def __init__(self, theme: Theme, image_width: int, size_of: SizeOf):

        self.width = image_width

"""
Drawing helpers for the guide's diagrams: cards, labelled boxes, arrows,
text and a stylised MRI slice (head, ventricles, lesion) that can show a
SAM box, a detection box, an outline or a filled region.

All coordinates are in "design units"; diagrams.py scales the painter so
diagrams stay sharp at any width.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Optional, Sequence

from PyQt5.QtCore import QPointF, QRectF, Qt
from PyQt5.QtGui import QBrush, QColor, QFont, QPainter, QPainterPath, QPen, QRadialGradient

from ..icons import pixmap
from ..theme import Theme

LESION_RED = QColor(255, 72, 72)
DETECT_GREEN = QColor(64, 220, 120)


def font(size: float, bold: bool = False) -> QFont:
    f = QFont()
    f.setPointSizeF(size)
    f.setBold(bold)
    return f


def card(p: QPainter, rect: QRectF, t: Theme) -> None:
    p.setPen(QPen(QColor(t.border), 1))
    p.setBrush(QColor(t.surface_alt))
    p.drawRoundedRect(rect, 12, 12)


def text(p: QPainter, rect: QRectF, value: str, color: str, size: float = 9.5, bold: bool = False,
         align=Qt.AlignCenter) -> None:
    p.setFont(font(size, bold))
    p.setPen(QColor(color))
    p.drawText(rect, int(align) | Qt.TextWordWrap, value)


def box(p: QPainter, rect: QRectF, t: Theme, icon: str, title: str, subtitle: str = "",
        accent: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    """Rounded tile: icon on top, bold title, muted subtitle."""
    color = accent or t.accent
    p.setPen(QPen(QColor(t.border_strong), 1))
    p.setBrush(QColor(t.raised))
    p.drawRoundedRect(rect, 10, 10)
    p.setPen(Qt.NoPen)
    tint = QColor(color)
    tint.setAlpha(40)
    p.setBrush(tint)
    circle = QRectF(rect.center().x() - 17, rect.top() + 12, 34, 34)
    p.drawEllipse(circle)
    p.drawPixmap(circle.adjusted(8, 8, -8, -8).toRect(), pixmap(icon, color, 36))
    text(p, QRectF(rect.left() + 4, rect.top() + 52, rect.width() - 8, 20), title, t.text, 9.5, True)
    if subtitle:
        text(p, QRectF(rect.left() + 6, rect.top() + 72, rect.width() - 12, rect.height() - 76),

```python
"""
Concept diagrams of the User Guide, drawn with QPainter in the current
theme's colors (so they suit both light and dark mode and stay sharp).

    render(name, width, theme, ratio) -> QPixmap
    DESIGN_SIZES[name]                -> (width, height) in design units
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, Tuple

from PyQt5.QtCore import QPointF, QRectF, Qt
from PyQt5.QtGui import QColor, QPainter, QPen, QPixmap

from ..theme import Theme
from .drawing import DETECT_GREEN, LESION_RED, arrow, box, card, chip, mri_slice, number, text

RED, YELLOW, GREEN = (255, 0, 0), (255, 255, 0), (0, 255, 0)
CUSTOM = (148, 103, 189)


def _workflow(p: QPainter, t: Theme) -> None:
    card(p, QRectF(0, 0, 760, 190), t)
    steps = [("folder-open", "Open scans", "a folder of DICOM slices"),
             ("tag", "Pick a label", "what you will outline"),
             ("sparkles", "Segment", "Auto Detect, a box, or draw"),
             ("save", "Check & save", "one _seg.dcm per slice"),
             ("layers", "Batch the rest", "blank & auto ranges"),
             ("bar-chart", "Review & measure", "viewer, volume, 3D")]
    x, w, gap = 14, 104, 20
    for i, (icon, title, sub) in enumerate(steps):
        rect = QRectF(x + i * (w + gap), 26, w, 128)
        box(p, rect, t, icon, title, sub)
        number(p, QPointF(rect.left() + 12, rect.top() + 12), i + 1, t.accent)
        if i < len(steps) - 1:
            arrow(p, rect.right() + 3, rect.center().y(), rect.right() + gap - 3, rect.center().y(), t.text_faint)
    text(p, QRectF(0, 160, 760, 22), "Most people repeat steps 2–4 slice by slice, then use steps 5 and 6.",
         t.text_muted, 8.5)


def _series(p: QPainter, t: Theme) -> None:
    card(p, QRectF(0, 0, 760, 230), t)
    for k in range(5):                                   # a stack of slices
        r = QRectF(40 + k * 14, 40 + k * 12, 120, 120)
        mri_slice(p, r, lesion=k in (2, 3), faint=k < 4)
    text(p, QRectF(20, 196, 230, 22), "A series = one folder of slices", t.text, 9.5, True)
    arrow(p, 260, 120, 320, 120, t.text_faint)
    mri_slice(p, QRectF(330, 50, 150, 150))
    text(p, QRectF(330, 30, 150, 18), "Slice 21 of 40", t.text_muted, 8.5)
    text(p, QRectF(320, 200, 170, 22), "You annotate one slice at a time", t.text, 9.5, True)
    arrow(p, 492, 120, 540, 120, t.text_faint)
    files = [("image", "demo_slice_021.dcm", "the image (never changed)", t.text_muted),
             ("tag", "demo_slice_021_seg.dcm", "your annotation, saved next to it", t.accent)]
    for k, (icon_name, name, note, color) in enumerate(files):
        y = 70 + k * 62
        p.setPen(QPen(QColor(t.border_strong), 1))
        p.setBrush(QColor(t.raised))
        p.drawRoundedRect(QRectF(552, y, 196, 50), 8, 8)
        from ..icons import pixmap
        p.drawPixmap(564, y + 15, pixmap(icon_name, color, 20))

"""The User Guide's table of contents: parts and their chapters, in reading order."""
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple

from . import part_annotate, part_reference, part_review, part_save, part_start, part_tools
from .chapter import Chapter

GROUPS: List[Tuple[str, List[Chapter]]] = [
    ("Getting started", part_start.CHAPTERS),
    ("Annotating", part_annotate.CHAPTERS),
    ("Saving & batch work", part_save.CHAPTERS),
    ("Reviewing & measuring", part_review.CHAPTERS),
    ("Advanced tools", part_tools.CHAPTERS),
    ("Reference", part_reference.CHAPTERS),
]

HOME = "welcome"


def all_chapters() -> List[Chapter]:
    return [chapter for _group, chapters in GROUPS for chapter in chapters]


def find(chapter_id: str) -> Optional[Chapter]:
    return next((c for c in all_chapters() if c.id == chapter_id), None)


def group_of(chapter_id: str) -> str:
    return next((g for g, chapters in GROUPS for c in chapters if c.id == chapter_id), "")


def neighbours(chapter_id: str) -> Tuple[Optional[Chapter], Optional[Chapter]]:
    chapters = all_chapters()
    ids = [c.id for c in chapters]
    if chapter_id not in ids:
        return None, None
    i = ids.index(chapter_id)
    return (chapters[i - 1] if i > 0 else None), (chapters[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(chapters) else None)
```

"""User Guide — Getting started."""
from .chapter import Chapter

WELCOME = Chapter(
    "welcome", "Welcome to DicomDoodle", "book",
    "A friendly tool for outlining lesions on MRI scans and saving them as standard medical files — "
    "no programming needed.",
    """
DicomDoodle helps you **mark (annotate) regions on MRI slices** — for example the edge of a brain tumour — and saves every annotation as a standard medical-imaging file that other software can read. Artificial intelligence (AI) does most of the drawing; you check it and correct it where needed.

![The whole journey in six steps](diagram:workflow)

## Who is it for?
- **Radiologists and clinicians** who want to mark findings quickly and consistently.
- **Researchers and students** preparing images for a study or for training AI models.
- **Anyone new to medical images** — every technical word is explained the first time it appears, and the [Glossary](chapter:glossary) collects them all.

## What you need
- A folder of **DICOM** files from one MRI series. DICOM is the standard file format of medical scanners; usually there is one file per slice.
- Nothing else: the AI models come with DicomDoodle. A computer with an NVIDIA graphics card (GPU) makes the AI faster, but everything also works without one.

> TRY IT: No scans at hand? Open the [demo series](action:demo) — a synthetic, computer-made head scan with one lesion. It contains no patient data, so you can experiment freely.

## How this guide is organised
| Part | What you will learn |
|---|---|
| Getting started | The main window, opening scans, moving through slices |
| Annotating | Labels and colors, AI segmentation, drawing by hand |
| Saving & batch work | What is saved, and how to process many slices at once |
| Reviewing & measuring | Checking saved work, standard medical terms, lesion volume |
| Advanced tools | 3D models, multiplanar views, file conversion, preferences |
| Reference | Keyboard shortcuts, troubleshooting, glossary |

> TIP: Press [[F1]] at any time to open this guide. Panels and tool windows have a {icon:help} button that opens the matching chapter directly.
""", "introduction overview start what is")

## 1. Open the demo series
1. On the start page, click **Try the demo series** — or [open it now](action:demo).
2. The 40 slices load in a second and the first slice appears in the middle of the window.

## 2. Find the lesion
1. Move the mouse over the image and **roll the mouse wheel** (or press [[→]]) to move through the slices.
2. Stop around **slice 21**: a bright ring appears in the upper right part of the head. That ring is the lesion you will outline.

## 3. Let the AI outline it

2. Click {icon:sparkles} **Auto Detect** in the toolbar, or press [[Ctrl+D]].
3. After a few seconds a red outline hugs the lesion, and a green dashed box shows where the AI found it. The badge at the top right of the image now reads **Unsaved changes**.

## 4. Save it
1. Click {icon:save} **Save**, or press [[Ctrl+S]].
2. A message confirms the file name — `demo_slice_021_seg.dcm` — and the badge turns green: **Saved**.

def plain_text(body: str) -> str:
    """Searchable text of a chapter (markup removed)."""
    text = re.sub(r"!\[(.*?)\]\(.*?\)", r"\1", body)
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)", r"\1", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\{(icon|n):[\w-]+\}", "", text)
    return re.sub(r"[#*`>\[\]|]", " ", text)

"""
Segmentation labels: the names, colors and pixel values used for annotation.

Every annotation is stored as a *label map*: a uint8 image where 0 is
background and any other number is the ``value`` of a :class:`SegLabel`.
When a slice is saved, each value becomes one segment of the DICOM SEG file,
named after the label (DICOM ``SegmentLabel``).

DicomDoodle ships six built-in labels — values 1-6, identical to the original
tool, so existing ``_seg.dcm`` files keep their meaning. Users can add their
own labels with any color; those get values 7, 8, ... and are stored in the

    def _applied(self, result) -> None:
        updated, errors = result
        if errors:
            show_error(self, "Some files were not updated", f"{len(errors)} problem(s):\n" + "\n".join(errors[:10]))
        else:
            show_info(self, "Success", f"Successfully processed {updated} annotation file(s).")
        self.applied.emit(updated)

    def _apply_failed(self, message: str, details: str) -> None:
        show_error(self, "Ontology", message, details)

    def export_csv(self) -> None:
        if not self.results:

        path, _ = QFileDialog.getSaveFileName(self, "Export results", "lesion_volumes.csv", "CSV (*.csv)")

    def _pick_and_load_series(self, title: str):
        folder = QFileDialog.getExistingDirectory(self, title, self.start_dir)
        if not folder:
            return None, None, None, None
        self.start_dir = os.path.dirname(folder)
        try:
            series_ids = mpr.find_series_ids(folder)
            if len(series_ids) > 1:
                item, ok = QInputDialog.getItem(self, "Multiple series found",
                                                "This folder contains more than one DICOM series.\nChoose one:",
                                                series_ids, 0, False)
                if not ok:
                    return None, None, None, None
                series_id = item
            else:
                series_id = series_ids[0] if series_ids else None
            QApplication.setOverrideCursor(Qt.WaitCursor)
            try:
                image = mpr.load_dicom_series(folder, series_id)
                try:
                    segmentation = self._load_segmentation(folder, image)
                except Exception:
                    segmentation = None   # an unreadable SEG must not block the image
            finally:
                QApplication.restoreOverrideCursor()

            "top-right": "bottom-left", "bottom-left": "top-right"}


def _corner_point(rect: QRectF, corner: str) -> QPointF:

class _Handle(QGraphicsRectItem):
    """A corner grip; ignores view scaling so it is always HANDLE_SIZE pixels."""

"""User Guide — Annotating."""
from .chapter import Chapter

LABELS = Chapter(
    "labels", "Labels and colors", "tag",
    "A label says *what* you outline. Pick one before you segment — each has its own color and name.",
    """
Every outline you make belongs to a **label**. The label decides the color on screen and the name stored in the annotation file, so anyone who opens the file later knows what the region means.

![A label in the panel becomes a named segment in the file](diagram:labels)

## The built-in labels
DicomDoodle comes with six labels — the same as the original DicomDoodle, so older annotation files keep their meaning. They cannot be changed or removed.

| | Shown as | Name saved in the file | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| {color:FF0000} | Tumor \\| Brain | Tumor & Brain Boundary | [[1]] |
| {color:00FF00} | Tumor \\| Dura | Tumor & Dura Boundary | [[2]] |
| {color:0000FF} | Tumor \\| Necrosis | Tumor & Necrosis Boundary | [[3]] |
| {color:FFFF00} | Edema \\| Brain | Edema & Brain Boundary | [[4]] |
| {color:00FFFF} | Tumor \\| Edema | Tumor & Edema Boundary | [[5]] |
| {color:FF00FF} | Magenta | Magenta Boundary | [[6]] |

## Choosing the active label
The **active label** is the one used for the next Auto Detect, box or batch run. It is highlighted in the **Labels** panel and shown at the bottom left of the image (*Label: …*).
- Click a label in the **Labels** panel, or
- press its number key [[1]] … [[9]] (the number is shown at the right of each label), or
- use **Annotate ▸ Active Label**.

> TIP: Change the label first, then segment. A region keeps the label it was made with.

## Adding your own label
You can add as many labels as you need — for example *Enhancing tumour*, *Cyst* or *Resection cavity* — with any color.
1. Click {icon:plus} **Add label** under the label list (or **Annotate ▸ Add Label…**). The **New label** window opens.
2. Type the **Name** — this exact text is saved in the annotation files, so make it clear and complete.
3. Optionally type a **Short name** for the label list (for example *Enh. Tumor*).
4. Pick a color: click one of the **Suggested colors** (colors no other label uses yet) or choose any color in the full **Color palette** on the right — by clicking, by typing RGB / HSV values or an HTML code like `#FF8C00`, or with **Pick Screen Color**.
5. Check the **Preview** and the message below it, then click **Create label**. The new label is selected right away.

![The New label window](shot:label_editor)

| | In the New label window |
|---|---|
| {n:1} | **Name** — saved in every annotation file that uses the label (up to 64 characters) |
| {n:2} | **Short name** — optional, shown in the label list |
| {n:3} | **Preview** and check: a red message explains what to fix; orange means the color looks like another label's |
| {n:4} | **Suggested colors** — one click picks a color nobody uses yet |
| {n:5} | **Colors already in use** — hover to see which label has which color |
| {n:6} | **Color palette** — every possible color, with a screen color picker |
| {n:7} | **Create label** — becomes available when the name and color are valid |

> NOTE: Names must be unique and colors must differ from the other labels, so regions can always be told apart.

## Editing, removing and sharing labels
- **Double-click** one of your labels to change its name or color, or use the {icon:sliders} menu next to **Add label** ▸ **Edit selected label…**.
- {icon:sliders} ▸ **Remove selected label** deletes one of your labels. Files already saved keep their segment names.
- {icon:sliders} ▸ **Export my labels…** saves your labels to a small `.json` file; a colleague can load it with **Import labels…** so the whole team uses identical names and colors.
- Right-click any label for the same commands.

```python
"""User Guide — Saving & batch work."""
from .chapter import Chapter

SAVING = Chapter(
    "saving", "Saving annotations", "save",
    "What is written to disk, where it goes, and how DicomDoodle protects your work.",
    """
## One annotation file per slice
When you save, DicomDoodle writes a new file **next to the slice**, with the same name plus `_seg.dcm`. The slice `demo_slice_021.dcm` gets `demo_slice_021_seg.dcm` in the same folder. The original image file is never changed.

The file is a **DICOM Segmentation** (*DICOM SEG*) — the official DICOM format for marked regions — so it stays linked to its slice and can be read by other medical-imaging software. Inside it:
- every label used on the slice becomes one **segment**, named with the label's full name (for example *Tumor & Brain Boundary*);
- each region is stored as its **outline** — a one-pixel boundary line — exactly like the original DicomDoodle. Small gaps of up to 20 pixels are closed automatically. DicomDoodle's viewer, volume calculator and 3D tools fill the outlines again when needed.

![Filled region, saved outline and blank mask](diagram:saved)

## Saving
- **This slice:** {icon:save} **Save** in the toolbar, or [[Ctrl+S]].
- **Every slice with unsaved changes:** **File ▸ Save All Modified Slices**, or [[Ctrl+Shift+S]]. A progress window shows each file being written.

## Blank masks: “I checked — no lesion here”
Saving a slice without any outline asks *Save blank mask?*. A blank mask is a valid annotation file that contains the segment *No Segmentation*. It records that the slice was checked and shows no lesion — which is different from a slice nobody has looked at yet. To save blank masks for many slices at once, see [Batch processing](chapter:batch).

## Is this slice saved?
The badge at the top right of the image always tells you:

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Unsaved changes** (orange) | The slice has work that is not saved yet. |
| **Saved** (green) | Saved during this session. |
| **Annotation file on disk** (blue) | A file from an earlier session exists. Turn on *Show saved annotation files* to see it. |

The ticks under the [slice timeline](chapter:viewing) show the same information for the whole series.

## Your work is protected
- Before you open another folder, close the series or quit with unsaved annotations, DicomDoodle asks: **Save all**, **Discard** or **Cancel**.
- Before replacing an annotation file from an earlier session, it asks first. Tick *Don't ask again* if you prefer; the question can be turned back on in **File ▸ Preferences ▸ Files**.
- Files are written to a temporary file first and renamed when complete, so an interrupted save never leaves a damaged file.

> NOTE: The Activity Log (**View ▸ Panels ▸ Activity Log**) lists every file saved in this session.
""", "save ctrl+s seg dcm file dicom seg segmentation blank mask outline boundary unsaved overwrite replace")

BATCH = Chapter(
    "batch", "Batch processing: many slices at once", "layers",
    "Save blank masks for slices without a lesion, and auto-detect a whole run of slices in one go.",
    """
In most series only some slices show the lesion. The **Batch Processing** panel on the right handles the rest quickly:
- **Blank masks** — up to two ranges of slices *without* a lesion (for example before and after it) each get an empty annotation file.
- **Auto-detect range** — every slice in the range is processed with [Auto Detect](chapter:auto-detect), and each result is saved straight away. Where nothing is found, a blank mask is saved.

![The Batch Processing panel](shot:batch)

| | |

| {n:1} | **Range 1** — Start and End buttons show the chosen slices |
| {n:2} | **Range 2** — a second blank range, for example after the lesion |
| {n:3} | **Save blank masks** — the number in brackets is how many slices will be saved |
| {n:4} | **Auto-detect range** with its own Start and End |
| {n:5} | The label the auto-detect results will get (the active label) |

Use the viewer to check a finished series, to show your annotations to a colleague, or to look at annotation files made by someone else.

## Opening it
Click {icon:layers} **Annotated DICOM Viewer** on the right of the toolbar (or **Tools ▸ Annotated DICOM Viewer**). If a series is open in the main window, the viewer opens it straight away; otherwise click **Load DICOM Folder**.

| {n:1} | **Load DICOM Folder** — any folder with slices and their annotation files |

| {n:3} | **Show Mask** — fills each closed outline with a color of its own |

| {n:7} | The annotation file(s) of this slice |

## Moving around
The controls are the same as in the main window: the mouse wheel or arrow keys change the slice, [[Ctrl]] + wheel zooms, the middle mouse button pans, and {icon:play} on the timeline plays the series as a film. Annotated slices are marked on the timeline.

## Which annotation files are shown
Some folders contain annotation files from two different tools — DicomDoodle's `_seg.dcm` and, for example, `_segmentation.dcm` from another program. Choose with **Annotation files**:
- **\\*_seg.dcm (DicomDoodle)** — only DicomDoodle's files,
- **\\*_segmentation.dcm** — only the other kind,
- **All annotation files (merged)** — both together.

ONTOLOGY = Chapter(

    """
A label name like *Tumor & Brain Boundary* is clear to people, but software needs a precise code. **Ontologies** are agreed lists of medical terms with codes — for example SNOMED CT or the NCI Thesaurus. **BioPortal** is a free online library of such ontologies.

DicomDoodle writes two terms into each annotation file:
- **Segment category** — the broad kind of thing, for example *Morphologically abnormal structure*;
- **Segment type** — the specific thing, for example *Glioma*.

## Step by step
1. Open the series in the [Annotated DICOM Viewer](chapter:viewer).
2. Click {icon:share} **Add Ontology** at the right of its toolbar. The **BioPortal Ontology Search** window opens.
3. Type a term (for example *glioma*) and press [[Enter]] or click **Get labels**. The first 10 results appear; **Show all results** lists the rest.
4. Click a result to see its details. **Definition & synonyms** explains what it means.
5. Click **Use as category** or **Use as type** (or right-click the result).
6. When both are chosen, click **Apply to files** and confirm. Every annotation file of the series is updated; blank masks get *Organ / Brain*.

```text
def collect_series_masks(slice_uids: Sequence[str], slice_instances: Sequence[Optional[int]],
                         seg_paths: Sequence[str], shape: Tuple[int, int],
                         progress: Optional[Progress] = None) -> Dict[int, np.ndarray]:
    """Union of all annotated pixels per slice index, across many SEG files.

    Frames are matched to slices by ReferencedSOPInstanceUID; files without
    that reference fall back to their InstanceNumber (as the original did).
    """
    progress = ensure_progress(progress)
    uid_to_index = {uid: i for i, uid in enumerate(slice_uids) if uid}
    instance_to_index = {inst: i for i, inst in enumerate(slice_instances) if inst is not None}
    masks: Dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}
    for k, path in enumerate(seg_paths):
        progress(k, len(seg_paths), "Reading annotations…")
        try:
            ds = pydicom.dcmread(path)
            frames = list(iter_frames(ds))
        except Exception as exc:
            log.warning("Skipping unreadable annotation %s: %s", path, exc)
            continue
        fallback = instance_to_index.get(int(ds.InstanceNumber)) if ds.get("InstanceNumber") else None
        for frame in frames:
            index = uid_to_index.get(frame.referenced_sop_uid, fallback)
            if index is None or not frame.mask.any():
                continue
            mask = frame.mask
            if mask.shape != tuple(shape):
                log.warning("Annotation %s does not match the slice size; skipped.", path)
                continue
            masks[index] = masks[index] | mask if index in masks else mask.copy()
    return masks

"""
Building the volumes shown by the 3D Model Viewer (port of the two
background workers in the original create_3d.py).

Up to three series folders (axial / coronal / sagittal) are read with
SimpleITK, resampled onto the grid of the first one available (axial
preferred) and averaged. Annotation files become a filled 3D lesion mask on
the same grid, and the lesion is brightened in the "anatomy" volume so it
stands out (FLAIR folders: lesion x1.4 and the rest x0.2; otherwise lesion
x1.99) — the original's rules.

Differences from the original: the series are read once instead of twice
(one worker per view), images are always resampled with linear interpolation
(the original switched to nearest-neighbour after the first mask), and
multi-label annotation frames stay on their own slice.
"""

        if not self.has_data:
            return
        smin, smax = self.data_range
        if smin == smax:

        smin, smax = max(smin, s.scalar_min), min(smax, s.scalar_max)
        if smin >= smax:

"""User Guide — Advanced tools."""
from .chapter import Chapter

VIEWER_3D = Chapter(
    "viewer3d", "3D Model Viewer", "cube",
    "See the head and the annotated lesion in 3D, turn it around, cut into it and measure the lesion.",
    """
The 3D Model Viewer stacks all slices of a series into a three-dimensional model. When the folders contain annotation files, the lesion is highlighted and measured.

## Building the 3D model
1. Click {icon:cube} **3D Model Viewer** on the right of the toolbar.
2. Click {icon:folder-open} **Load Series…**. Choose up to three folders of the **same patient** — axial, coronal and/or sagittal (the open series is filled in for you).
3. Choose which **Annotation files** to use, then click **Process 3D Plot**. Building the model takes a few seconds.

![The 3D Model Viewer with the demo series](shot:viewer3d)

| | |
|---|---|
| {n:1} | **Load Series…** — choose the folders |
| {n:2} | **Reset Cameras** — back to the starting view |
| {n:3} | **Link Views** — turn and zoom both views together |
| {n:4} | Settings for each view, on two tabs |
| {n:5} | **Anatomy & lesion** — the lesion is made brighter so it stands out |
| {n:6} | **Volume** — the plain 3D image |
| {n:7} | **Lesion metrics** calculated from the annotation files |
| {n:8} | **Show lesion surface in 3D** — the lesion as a red, see-through surface |

## Moving the model
- **Left-drag** turns the model, **right-drag** or the **mouse wheel** zooms, **middle-drag** moves it.
- {icon:refresh} above each view resets its camera; {icon:camera} saves a picture of the view (PNG).

## Settings (left panel)
- **Appearance** — the **Colormap** (13 color schemes, from *Grayscale* to *BrainTumorSpecific*), **Contrast**, **Ambience** (overall light), **Opacity threshold** (hides faint tissue), **Gradient opacity** (makes edges stand out), **Specular power** (shine), and **Scalar min / max** (the brightness range shown).
- **Surgery planning** — **Edge enhancement**, **Tissue density**, **Advanced shading**, and **Show lesion surface & metrics**.
- **Clipping planes** — tick **X**, **Y** or **Z axis** and move the slider to cut the model open and look inside.
- **Lighting** — the direction (**Azimuth**, **Elevation**) and **Intensity** of the light.
- **Reset to defaults** restores the settings of that view.

## Lesion metrics
| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Volume (cc)** | Lesion volume; 1 cc = 1 cm³ = 1 millilitre |
| **Surface Area (mm²)** | The area of the lesion's outer surface |
| **Sphericity** | How round the lesion is: 1 = a perfect ball, lower = more irregular |
| **Texture Contrast** | How much the brightness varies inside the lesion |
| **Texture Homogeneity** | How even the brightness is inside the lesion |

> NOTE: The viewer needs the optional packages *vtk* and *SimpleITK*. If they are missing, DicomDoodle says so when you open it.

```python
"""User Guide — Reference: shortcuts, troubleshooting, glossary."""
import re

from .chapter import Chapter
from .shortcuts import SHORTCUTS


def _keys(text: str) -> str:
    """'Ctrl+Z  /  Ctrl+Y' -> '[[Ctrl+Z]] / [[Ctrl+Y]]' (markup key chips)."""
    def chip(key: str) -> str:
        return "[[" + re.sub(r"([\[\]|])", r"\\\1", key.strip()) + "]]"
    parts = re.split(r"(\s+/\s+|\s+or\s+)", text)
    return "".join(f" {p.strip()} " if i % 2 else chip(p) for i, p in enumerate(parts))


def _shortcuts_body() -> str:
    lines = ["Everything you can do with the keyboard and mouse. The same list is in **Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts**.", ""]
    for group, rows in SHORTCUTS:
        lines += [f"## {group}", "| Keys | What it does |", "|---|---|"]
        lines += [f"| {_keys(keys)} | {action} |" for keys, action in rows]
        lines.append("")
    lines.append("> TIP: Number keys and arrows act on the image, not while you type in a text or number box.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


SHORTCUTS_CHAPTER = Chapter(
    "shortcuts", "Keyboard and mouse shortcuts", "keyboard",
    "Work faster: every shortcut in one list.",
    _shortcuts_body(), "keys keyboard shortcut hotkey mouse wheel")

TROUBLESHOOTING = Chapter(
    "troubleshooting", "Troubleshooting and questions", "help",
    "Answers to the questions people ask most.",
    """
### The AI takes a long time the first time
The models are loaded into memory the first time you use them in a session — a few seconds, up to a minute on slow computers. After that each slice takes about a second with a graphics card (GPU), longer on the processor (CPU). To load SAM while you are still opening files, tick *Load SAM in the background* in **File ▸ Preferences ▸ AI Models**.

### “AI model error” or “weights not found”
DicomDoodle needs three model files: `best_flair.pt`, `yoloe-11l-seg-pf.pt` and `sam2.1_l.pt`. **File ▸ Preferences ▸ AI Models** shows which ones were found; point **Models folder** at the folder that contains them.

### “No detection found for this slice”
The detector did not recognise a lesion — common on slices where it is very small. Draw a box around it ([Segment with a box](chapter:box)) or draw it by hand ([Manual Draw](chapter:manual-draw)).

### The outline covers too much, or the wrong structure
Undo with [[Ctrl+Z]], draw a tighter box around just the lesion and press [[Enter]] again. For fine corrections use [Manual Draw](chapter:manual-draw).

### My folder opens, but some files are missing
Annotation files are never shown as slices, and files that are not images (reports, for example) are skipped. Open **View ▸ Panels ▸ Activity Log** to see which files were skipped and why. A series stored as a single file must be split first with the [Multi-frame Converter](chapter:converter).

### A tool says “Tool unavailable”
That tool needs an optional Python package (for example *vtk*, *SimpleITK* or *matplotlib*). The message names it; install everything at once with `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

### The ontology search does not work
It needs an internet connection and a valid BioPortal key (**File ▸ Preferences ▸ Ontology**). Firewalls in some hospitals block the BioPortal website.

### Where are my annotation files?
In the same folder as the slices, named `<slice name>_seg.dcm` — see [Saving annotations](chapter:saving). The **Series Info** tab shows the folder.

### Can I change an annotation after saving it?
Yes. Annotate the slice again and save — or correct it with **Manual Draw ▸ Load Annotation**. The file is replaced; DicomDoodle asks first if it is from an earlier session.

"""
Turns a guide chapter written in a small markup into HTML for QTextBrowser,
colored with the current theme.

Blocks (one per line):
    ## Heading   /   ### Subheading
    plain lines              paragraph (a blank line ends it)
    1. text                  numbered step
    - text                   bullet
    > TIP: text              callout box: TIP, NOTE, IMPORTANT or TRY IT
                             (following "> " lines continue the same box)
    ![Caption](shot:name)    screenshot (dicomdoodle/assets/guide/name.png);
                             clicking it opens it full size
    ![Caption](diagram:x)    diagram drawn by ui/guide/diagrams.py
    | a | b |                table row (the first row is the header)

Inline:
    **bold**  *italic*  `file name`  [[Ctrl+S]] key  {icon:save} toolbar icon
    {n:3} numbered marker (as drawn on the screenshots)   {color:FF0000} swatch
    [text](chapter:id)  [text](action:name)  [text](https://...)
    \\| \\[ \\] \\* ...         a literal character (e.g. a "|" inside a table cell)

Images are referenced by URL (e.g. ``shot:overview@760~dark``); the guide
window supplies them in ``loadResource`` at exactly the requested width.
The ``~theme`` suffix makes the document fetch new images after a theme
change instead of reusing cached ones.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import re
from typing import Callable, List, Optional, Tuple

from ..theme import Theme, rgba

SizeOf = Callable[[str], Tuple[int, int]]          # "shot:name" -> natural (w, h)

CALLOUTS = {   # kind -> (icon, theme token)
    "TIP": ("sparkles", "accent"),
    "NOTE": ("info", "text_muted"),
    "IMPORTANT": ("alert", "warning"),
    "TRY IT": ("play", "success"),
}

_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\\([\\\[\]|*`{}#>!-])")
_CELL_SPLIT = re.compile(r"(?<!\\)\|")


def split_resource(url: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """'shot:overview@760~dark' -> ('shot:overview@760', 'dark')."""
    base, _, tag = url.partition("~")
    return base, tag

# DicomDoodle 2 — modular application

A redesigned DicomDoodle with a modern interface, light and dark themes,
unlimited custom labels, and a code base split into small, focused modules.
Every feature of the original tool is here, and annotation files are fully
compatible with the original: same `<slice>_seg.dcm` DICOM Segmentation
files, same segment names, same pixel content.

## Run it

```bash
cd DicomDoodle/DicomDoodle_App
pip install -r requirements.txt      # once
python main.py                       # or: python main.py "path/to/dicom folder"
```

The AI model weights (`sam2.1_l.pt`, `best_flair.pt`, `yoloe-11l-seg-pf.pt`),
the logo images and the PDF manual are found automatically in the parent
`DicomDoodle/` folder — nothing is copied. Another weights folder can be
chosen in **File ▸ Preferences ▸ AI Models**.

+def paint_marker(p: QPainter, center: QPointF, label: str, radius: float, color: str = CALLOUT_ORANGE,
+                 ring: bool = True) -> None:
+    """Numbered disc: white ring and soft shadow (readable on any image), white number."""
+    p.save()
+    p.setRenderHint(QPainter.Antialiasing)
+    p.setPen(Qt.NoPen)
+    inner = radius
+    if ring:
+        p.setBrush(QColor(0, 0, 0, 80))
+        p.drawEllipse(center + QPointF(0, radius * 0.1), radius + 0.8, radius + 0.8)
+        p.setBrush(QColor("#ffffff"))
+        p.drawEllipse(center, radius, radius)
+        inner = radius * 0.84
+    p.setBrush(QColor(color))
+    p.drawEllipse(center, inner, inner)
+    f = QFont()
+    f.setBold(True)
+    f.setPixelSize(max(6, int(round(radius * (1.0 if len(label) < 2 else 0.85)))))
+    p.setFont(f)
+    p.setPen(QColor("#ffffff"))
+    p.drawText(QRectF(center.x() - radius, center.y() - radius, 2 * radius, 2 * radius), Qt.AlignCenter, label)
+    p.restore()
+
+
+def marker_pixmap(label: str, size: int, ratio: float, color: str = CALLOUT_ORANGE, ring: bool = True) -> QPixmap:
+    out = QPixmap(int(round(size * ratio)), int(round(size * ratio)))
+    out.fill(Qt.transparent)
+    p = QPainter(out)
+    p.scale(ratio, ratio)
+    paint_marker(p, QPointF(size / 2, size / 2), label, size / 2 - (1.2 if ring else 0.5), color, ring)
+    p.end()
+    out.setDevicePixelRatio(ratio)
+    return out
+
+
+def swatch_pixmap(hex_color: str, size: int, ratio: float, border: str) -> QPixmap:
+    out = QPixmap(int(round(size * ratio)), int(round(size * ratio)))
+    out.fill(Qt.transparent)
+    p = QPainter(out)
+    p.setRenderHint(QPainter.Antialiasing)
+    p.scale(ratio, ratio)
+    p.setPen(QPen(QColor(border), 1))
+    p.setBrush(QColor(f"#{hex_color}"))
+    p.drawRoundedRect(QRectF(1, 1, size - 2, size - 2), 4, 4)
+    p.end()
+    out.setDevicePixelRatio(ratio)

```python
"""
The built-in, illustrated User Guide (it replaces the PDF manual).

    configure(settings, on_action)   once, by the main window
    show_guide("labels")             open the guide at a chapter (one window, reused)
    help_button("batch")             small (?) button that opens a chapter
    close_guide()                    when the app closes

The chapters themselves are text in ``dicomdoodle/help/``; this package
renders them: markup.py (text -> HTML), diagrams.py + drawing.py (pictures
drawn in the theme's colors) and window.py (the guide window).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Optional

from PyQt5.QtWidgets import QToolButton

from ..qt_utils import make_tool_button

_window = None
_settings = None
_on_action: Optional[Callable[[str], None]] = None


def configure(settings=None, on_action: Optional[Callable[[str], None]] = None) -> None:
    """``on_action(name)`` runs links such as "Open the demo series" in the main window."""
    global _settings, _on_action
    _settings, _on_action = settings, on_action


def _dispatch(name: str) -> None:
    if _on_action is not None:
        _on_action(name)


def show_guide(topic: str = ""):
    """Show the guide; ``topic`` is a chapter id (empty: stay where the reader was)."""
    global _window
    from .window import GuideWindow
    if _window is None:
        _window = GuideWindow(_settings)
        _window.actionRequested.connect(_dispatch)
    if topic:
        _window.show_chapter(topic)
    _window.showNormal()
    _window.raise_()
    _window.activateWindow()
    return _window


def close_guide() -> None:
    if _window is not None:
        _window.close()


def help_button(topic: str, tooltip: str = "Help on this — opens the User Guide") -> QToolButton:
    button = make_tool_button("help", tooltip, size=16)
    button.clicked.connect(lambda: show_guide(topic))
    return button

           "shortcuts", "references", "about", "add_label", "theme"}
ids = {c.id for c in contents.all_chapters()}

        if kind == "diagram" and target not in diagrams.DIAGRAMS: problems.append(f"{c.id}: bad diagram {target}")
        if kind == "shot": shots.add(target)
    for name in re.findall(r"\{icon:([\w-]+)\}", c.body + c.summary):

        for leftover in ("**", "[[", "]]", "{icon:", "{n:", "{color:", "](", "\\|", "\\["):

print("search 'blank mask' ->", [m.id for m in w.matches])

print("search nonsense ->", [m.id for m in w.matches], w.browser.toPlainText()[:80].replace("\n", " | "))
print("\n".join(problems) or "NO PROBLEMS")

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Chapter:
    id: str            # used in links: [text](chapter:id)
    title: str
    icon: str          # icon name from ui/icons.py

''')

shorts = {
    "part_start.py": {"quick-start": "Quick start (5 minutes)", "viewing": "Moving through slices"},
    "part_annotate.py": {"auto-detect": "Auto Detect (AI)", "correcting": "Checking & correcting"},
    "part_save.py": {"batch": "Batch processing"},
    "part_review.py": {"viewer": "Reviewing annotations", "ontology": "Standard terms (ontology)",
                       "volume": "Lesion volume"},
    "part_tools.py": {"mpr": "Multiplanar view", "converter": "Multi-frame files"},
    "part_reference.py": {"shortcuts": "Shortcuts", "troubleshooting": "Troubleshooting & FAQ"},
}
for name, mapping in shorts.items():
    p = f"dicomdoodle/help/{name}"
    s = open(p).read()
    for cid, short in mapping.items():
        # the keywords argument closes each Chapter(...): add short= after it
        pattern = re.compile(r'(\n    "' + re.escape(cid) + r'", .*?""", "[^"]*")\)', re.S)
        s, n = pattern.subn(lambda m: m.group(1) + f', short="{short}")', s, count=1)
        if n != 1:
            # chapters whose keywords line differs (shortcuts uses _shortcuts_body())
            pattern = re.compile(r'(\n    "' + re.escape(cid) + r'", .*?, "[^"\n]*")\)', re.S)
            s, n = pattern.subn(lambda m: m.group(1) + f', short="{short}")', s, count=1)
        print(name, cid, n)
    open(p, "w").write(s)

```python
"""
References & Citations: how to cite DicomDoodle, and the papers and
software it builds on, grouped by topic.

Each reference shows what DicomDoodle uses it for, an APA-style citation
with a clickable DOI, and copy buttons; everything can be copied at once or
exported as a BibTeX file. The entries live in ``help/references.py``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
from typing import List, Tuple

from PyQt5.QtCore import Qt, QTimer
from PyQt5.QtWidgets import (QApplication, QDialog, QFileDialog, QFrame, QHBoxLayout, QLabel, QLineEdit,
                             QPushButton, QScrollArea, QVBoxLayout, QWidget)

from ... import APP_NAME
from ...help.references import SECTIONS, Reference, all_references, app_reference, bibtex_file, plain_text
from ..icons import icon, pixmap
from ..qt_utils import label, make_button, show_error
from ..theme import current_theme


def citation_html(ref: Reference) -> str:
    """APA-style citation with the venue in italics and a clickable DOI / URL."""
    title = ref.title if ref.title.endswith((".", "?", "!")) else ref.title + "."
    venue = f"<i>{html.escape(ref.venue)}</i>" + (f", {html.escape(ref.details)}" if ref.details else "") + "."
    link = f' <a href="{ref.link}">{html.escape(ref.link)}</a>' if ref.link else ""
    return f"{html.escape(ref.author_text())} ({ref.year}). {html.escape(title)} {venue}{link}"


def _copy(button: QPushButton, text: str) -> None:
    """Put ``text`` on the clipboard; the button says “Copied” for a moment."""
    QApplication.clipboard().setText(text)
    caption = button.text()
    if caption.startswith("Copied"):
        return
    button.setText("Copied ✓")
    QTimer.singleShot(1400, lambda: button.setText(caption) if not _deleted(button) else None)


def _deleted(widget: QWidget) -> bool:
    try:
        widget.objectName()
        return False
    except RuntimeError:
        return True


class _ReferenceCard(QFrame):
    def __init__(self, ref: Reference, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.setObjectName("RefCard")
        self.ref = ref
        self.search_text = " ".join([ref.component, ref.role, ref.text(), ref.key]).lower()

        name = label(ref.component, "Heading")
        role = label(ref.role, "Muted", wrap=True)
        citation = QLabel(citation_html(ref))

from PyQt5.QtWidgets import (QAction, QCheckBox, QDockWidget, QFormLayout, QMainWindow, QScrollArea, QSizePolicy,
                             QSplitter, QTabWidget, QToolBar, QVBoxLayout, QWidget)
"""
DicomDoodle — MRI DICOM annotation, segmentation and visualization studio.

Package layout (README.md has the full module map):

    dicomdoodle/
        app.py        builds the QApplication, splash screen and main window
        resources.py  finds model weights, images and the guide's screenshots
        settings.py   persistent user preferences (JSON file)
        core/         pure Python logic: DICOM I/O, labels, masks, AI models ...
        workers/      background-thread helpers so the GUI never freezes
        ui/           everything Qt: theme, widgets, dialogs and tool windows
"""

APP_NAME = "DicomDoodle"
APP_VERSION = "2.0.0"
APP_TAGLINE = "MRI DICOM Annotation & Visualization Studio"
AUTHOR = "Pushp Lochan Kumar"
AUTHOR_EMAIL = "pushpl@iisc.ac.in"
# DicomDoodle 2 — Python 3.10+
PyQt5
numpy
pydicom
highdicom
opencv-python
scipy
scikit-image
SimpleITK
vtk
matplotlib
ultralytics          # YOLO / YOLOE / SAM (installs torch)

# Optional extras
# ontoportal-client  # not required any more: BioPortal is called directly when it is missing
# antspyx            # ANTsPy registration engine in the Multiplanar view
# cupy / cucim       # GPU acceleration of volume processing in the Multiplanar view

def _warm_up_models(window, models) -> None:
    from .workers import run_task

    window.set_ai_status("loading", "Loading SAM…")
    log = logging.getLogger("dicomdoodle")

    def ready(device: str) -> None:
        window.set_ai_status("ready", f"AI ready · {device}")
        log.info("SAM model loaded (%s)", device)

    def failed(message: str, _details: str) -> None:
        window.set_ai_status("error", "AI models unavailable")
        log.warning("Could not preload SAM: %s", message.splitlines()[0])

    run_task(lambda _ctx: models.warm_up(), on_result=ready, on_error=failed)

mask = m.segment_box(img, box)
inter = (mask & lesion[mid - 1]).sum(); union = (mask | lesion[mid - 1]).sum()
print("SAM mask px", int(mask.sum()), "IoU vs GT %.2f" % (inter / max(union, 1)))

## How the code is organised

```
DicomDoodle_App/
├── main.py                    entry point (python main.py)
└── dicomdoodle/
    ├── app.py                 builds QApplication, theme, splash, logging, main window
    ├── resources.py           finds model weights, images and the manual
    ├── settings.py            JSON preferences
    │
    ├── core/                  pure logic — no Qt widgets, usable from scripts
    │   ├── labels.py          SegLabel + LabelRegistry (built-in + user labels)
    │   ├── dicom_series.py    load a folder of slices; annotation file naming
    │   ├── seg_io.py          write / read DICOM SEG files (original format)
    │   ├── gap_fill.py        original boundary gap-closing algorithm
    │   ├── mask_ops.py        boundaries, contours, overlays
    │   ├── annotation.py      per-slice label maps with undo/redo, batch ranges
    │   ├── ai_models.py       YOLO / YOLOE / SAM model manager
    │   ├── ontology.py        BioPortal search, DICOM coded concepts
    │   ├── volume_calculator.py, multiframe.py, reconstruction3d.py, tumor_metrics.py
    │   ├── processing/        skull strip, z-score, connected components (MPR)
    │   └── mpr/               MPR volumes, loading, registration, SEG transfer
… 21 lines omitted …
  `fn` receives a progress context as its first argument; pass it to core functions
  as their `progress` parameter so Cancel works.
* **Connect long-lived signals (`themeChanged`, `labelsChanged`) to bound methods**,
  not lambdas, so Qt disconnects them when a window closes.
* **Colors come from the theme** (`theme_color("accent")`, QSS object names such as
  `Card`, `Muted`, `SectionTitle`, and `set_role(button, "primary")`).
* **Labels:** pixel values 1–6 are the original labels and must not change;
  user labels start at 7. `LabelRegistry.name_for(value)` gives the DICOM segment name.
* A new tool window: add a module under `ui/tools/`, then one method in
  `ui/main/tools.py` and one action in `ui/main/actions.py`.
````

  for every background: a five-minute Quick Start, one chapter per feature with

import os
import sys
import tempfile

import numpy as np
import pydicom
from pydicom.dataset import FileDataset, FileMetaDataset
from pydicom.uid import ExplicitVRLittleEndian, MRImageStorage, generate_uid

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from dicomdoodle.core import mask_ops  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.annotation import AnnotationSession, SliceAnnotation  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.dicom_series import DicomSeries, SegFileFilter, seg_path_for  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.labels import LabelError, LabelRegistry  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.seg_io import read_segmentation, write_segmentation  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.volume_calculator import compute_orientation_volume  # noqa: E402

SIZE, SLICES = 64, 4


def make_series(folder: str) -> None:
    """Write SLICES synthetic axial MR slices (out of order on disk)."""
    study, series, frame = generate_uid(), generate_uid(), generate_uid()
    for k in reversed(range(SLICES)):
        meta = FileMetaDataset()
        meta.MediaStorageSOPClassUID = MRImageStorage
        meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID = generate_uid()
        meta.TransferSyntaxUID = ExplicitVRLittleEndian
        ds = FileDataset(None, {}, file_meta=meta, preamble=b"\0" * 128)
        ds.SOPClassUID, ds.SOPInstanceUID = MRImageStorage, meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID
        ds.StudyInstanceUID, ds.SeriesInstanceUID, ds.FrameOfReferenceUID = study, series, frame
        ds.Modality, ds.PatientName, ds.PatientID = "MR", "Test^Patient", "T1"
        ds.Manufacturer, ds.ManufacturerModelName = "Test", "Synthetic"
        ds.InstanceNumber = k + 1

def test_annotation_history_and_ranges():
    ann = SliceAnnotation((8, 8))
    mask = np.zeros((8, 8), bool)
    mask[2:4, 2:4] = True
    ann.paint(mask, 3)
    assert ann.dirty and ann.can_undo and ann.label_map.sum() == 12
    ann.undo()
    assert ann.is_empty and ann.can_redo
    ann.redo()
    assert not ann.is_empty

    class FakeSeries:
        def __len__(self):
            return 10
    session = AnnotationSession.__new__(AnnotationSession)
    AnnotationSession.__init__(session, FakeSeries())
    session.blank_ranges[0].start, session.blank_ranges[0].end = 5, 2
    session.blank_ranges[1].start, session.blank_ranges[1].end = 4, 7
    assert session.blank_targets() == [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name, test in list(globals().items()):
        if name.startswith("test_") and callable(test):
            test()
            print(f"ok  {name}")

"""
Tests for the help content: the User Guide chapters, their markup, the
references and the demo series.

    python -m pytest tests          (or simply: python tests/test_help.py)
"""
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from dicomdoodle import resources  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.core.demo_data import (PIXEL_SPACING, SLICE_THICKNESS, ensure_demo_series,  # noqa: E402
                                        is_demo_series, phantom_volume)
from dicomdoodle.core.dicom_series import DicomSeries  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.help import contents  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.help.references import all_references, app_reference, bibtex_file  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.ui.guide.markup import Renderer, plain_text  # noqa: E402
from dicomdoodle.ui.theme import DARK  # noqa: E402

# links of the form action:<name> that the main window knows (ui/main/tools.py, guide_action)
ACTIONS = {"demo", "open", "overlay", "viewer3d", "mpr", "volume", "converter", "manual", "preferences",
           "shortcuts", "references", "about", "add_label", "theme"}


def test_chapters_and_links():
    chapters = contents.all_chapters()
    ids = [c.id for c in chapters]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "chapter ids must be unique"
    assert contents.HOME in ids
    for chapter in chapters:
        for kind, target in re.findall(r"\]\((chapter|action|shot):([\w-]+)\)", chapter.body):
            if kind == "chapter":
                assert target in ids, f"{chapter.id}: link to unknown chapter {target}"
            elif kind == "action":
                assert target in ACTIONS, f"{chapter.id}: unknown action {target}"
            else:
                path = os.path.join(resources.GUIDE_DIR, f"{target}.png")
                assert os.path.isfile(path), f"{chapter.id}: screenshot {target}.png is missing"
    first, last = chapters[0], chapters[-1]
    assert contents.neighbours(first.id)[0] is None and contents.neighbours(last.id)[1] is None


def test_markup_renders_every_chapter():
    renderer = Renderer(DARK, 760, lambda source: (760, 400))
    for chapter in contents.all_chapters():
        html = renderer.chapter("Part", chapter.title, chapter.summary, chapter.body)
        text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", html)
        for leftover in ("**", "[[", "]]", "{icon:", "{n:", "{color:", "](", "\\|"):
            assert leftover not in text, f"{chapter.id}: unrendered markup {leftover!r}"
        assert plain_text(chapter.body).strip()


def test_markup_details():
    renderer = Renderer(DARK, 600, lambda source: (1200, 600))
    rows = "".join(renderer.blocks("| Key | Label |\n|---|---|\n| [[1]] | Tumor \\| Brain |"))
    assert "Tumor | Brain" in rows and rows.count("<tr>") == 2
